profile.headline: ML Compiler Engineer at Microsoft
profile.summary:
I am a machine learning compilers engineer. I'm passionate about machine learning, computer systems, programming languages and compilers. 
 
I live in Seattle, WA, and my hobbies include hiking, backpacking, biking, skiing, urban foraging, salsa dancing,  knitting, and ceramics.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: I am an ML compiler engineer working on the compiler for Microsoft's MAIA chip. I lead the correctness effort for our semaphore graph, focusing on compiler infrastructure, reliability and maintainability. I closely collaborate with our performance and coverage teams to support performant new models.

positions.title: ML Compiler Engineer
positions.description:
Modular AI is rebuilding AI infrastructure for everyone.

The next generation of product breakthroughs will be powered by production quality infrastructure that brings together the best of compilers and runtimes, is designed for heterogeneous compute, edge to datacenter distribution, and is focused on usability. Unifying software and hardware with a "just works" approach that will save developers enormous time and increase their velocity.*

We are incredibly excited about the mission before us and if you are interested in joining us change the world - just reach out via www.modular.ai. We’re hiring everywhere. The future is super exciting and bright!

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Software engineer on the core compiler team. The majority of my work was contributing to TVM, an open source machine learning compiler. I worked on the ONNX importer, dynamic shapes and quantization. I also worked on improvements to the main part of the compiler, including changing lowering to be pass-based instead of ad-hoc and introducing an operation to call lowered functions, which makes it much easier to analyze calls.
You can view my contributions to TVM here: https://github.com/apache/tvm/pulls/electriclilies

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
Interned at Azure PIE (Production Infrastructure Engineering). Designed and implemented a prototype Troubleshooting Guide Assistant, a tool to help on-call employees find troubleshooting guides, as well as gather data about how troubleshooting guides are being used. 

I designed a data structure to store troubleshooting guides as decision trees, inspired by my work in programming languages. I implemented a browser extension for Orb, a chromium browser that is integrated with internal Microsoft tooling that on-call employees use frequently, that displays the troubleshooting guides using recursive pattern matching. (Javascript does not have built-in pattern-matching, so I implemented a version of it myself). Finally, I implemented a system so users can search for troubleshooting guides directly from the browser extension. The extension then retrieves the correct troubleshooting guide from a SQL database according to the user's search.

positions.title: Food Coordinator (2018-2019), Transportation Coordinator (2017-2018)
positions.description:
As transportation coordinator, I helped organize the team's transportation to and from meets by coordinating team member's vehicles and booking zipcars. 
As food coordinator, I will be in charge of purchasing, transporting and preparing food for 20+ people for our weekend meets. I will also organize team members to help cook the food once at our meet. In the past, we have invited other teams over for dinner at meets. I will organize these dinners as well.

positions.title: Summer Researcher
positions.description:
As an undergraduate researcher at the HCR lab, I helped develop Code-It, a block-based language for controlling robots. Code-It is a concurrent language that enables the user to control the robot simply and efficiently.
This work involved programming in C++ and JavaScript, as well as using ROS (Robotics Operating System) and Google's Blockly (a framework for creating block-based programming languages). 
I specifically worked on Code-It for Fetch robots, and implemented several sensing blocks -- for example, a block that detects whether an item has slipped from the robot's grasp, and blocks that detect and process speech input to the robot.

positions.title: Summer Intern (Robotics in the Real World REU)
positions.description:
I worked with Yigit Menguc, a robotics professor at Oregon State University, on pneumatically actuated soft snake robots. I fabricated the snakes and wrote scripts in Python to control the snakes. 
My major contribution to the design of the soft snakes included adding an inextensible backbone and experimenting with adding scale structures to improve speed and locomotion. 
I also used a professional 3d motion capture system to determine the best gait on various surfaces, and analyzed data acquired from the motion capture system using Python.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: During a half-credit independent study through the physics department, I helped build a florescence correlation spectroscopy microscope with physics professor Jerome Fung. My work on the project included machining parts for the optical system, purchasing and installing lenses, and aligning lasers.

positions.title: Summer Intern (UW Nanopore Lab)
positions.description:
I worked with Jens Gundlach in the University of Washington's physics department. His lab investigates the properties of MspA, a protein nanopore, and uses these pores to read DNA sequences and investigate the properties of enzymes that traverse DNA. 
I mixed cleaned lab equipment, buffer solution, created phospholipid bilayers, and ran experiments.

positions.title: Community Conversations Fascilitator
positions.description: I led discussions about various social issues including race, gender, and sexuality with my peers in high school. I developed public speaking and communication skills, and learned how to engage other students in discussions that were often uncomfortable.

positions.title: UWIN High School Fellow at the Moritz Lab
positions.description: I was employed as a UWIN High School Fellow at the Moritz lab in the University of Washington's department of rehabilitation medicine. I designed and fabricated an interactive wearable headpiece to restore proprioception to stroke patients. As a part of this project, I wrote code in C++ and Arduino IDE, and designed circuits.
